title: Observations of sulfuretted species in HL Tau
question: Investigate the chemical differences between the protoplanetary disk and the surrounding envelope of HL Tau by comparing column density ratios of CS, H2CO, H2S, and SO2.

evidence.quote: Table notes: Molecular data from CDMS (cite: Muller2005).

what.value: ALMA SO2 transition detections toward HL Tau
Collisional rates for CS, H2S, and H2CO

evidence.quote: We derived critical densities for the studied transitions using the Einstein coefficients for spontaneous emission from Table [\[Tab:line_fluxes\]](#Tab:line_fluxes) and collisional rates from (cite: DenisAlpizar2013) for CS, (cite: Dagdigian2020) for H$\rm _2$S, and (cite: Wiesenfeld2013) for H$\rm _2$CO.

recipe.goal: Compute moment maps, Keplerian-masked maps, line fluxes, and radial profiles for CS, H2S, and H2CO
recipe.method: Spectrally smooth cubes by a factor of 3, compute moment 0, 1, 2 maps (S/N > 4), apply Keplerian masks using bettermoments and make_mask, integrate fluxes within r = 1.6 arcsec masking out absorption, and compute deprojected azimuthally averaged radial profiles.
key_parameters: S/N > 4 threshold for unmasked moment maps; spectral smoothing factor = 3; integration radius = 1.6 arcsec
assumptions: M_star = 2.1 M_sun, i = 46.7 deg, PA = 138 deg

recipe.goal: Measure SO2 line fluxes and perform rotational diagram analysis combining NOEMA and ALMA transitions
recipe.method: Integrate SO2 emission inside the beam area of the 4(2,2)-4(1,3) transition centered on its peak, recompute ALMA fluxes from Garufi et al. (2022), and fit a rotational diagram for T_rot and N(SO2).
key_parameters: Partition function computed for 198 rotational levels
assumptions: Optically thin emission and Rayleigh-Jeans limit

recipe.goal: Derive molecular column densities and ratios in the envelope and protoplanetary disk
recipe.method: Compute optical depth and column density in the envelope from central absorption features for T_ex = 5 K and T_ex -> 0 K; compute LTE optically thin column densities in the disk at CS, H2S, and H2CO peaks and disk mean for T = 20, 40, and 58 K.
key_parameters: Envelope T_ex = 5 K and T_ex -> 0 K; Disk T = 20 K, 40 K, and 58 K; ortho-to-para correction factor of 1.33 (OPR = 3) for H2S and H2CO
assumptions: Continuum source fills the beam for absorption; LTE and optically thin emission in the disk; ortho-to-para ratio of 3 for H2S and H2CO
